eligibility_rule: An observation is eligible at decision instant D only when receipt_ms + recorded_uncertainty_ms <= D_ms AND recorded_uncertainty_ms <= max_clock_uncertainty_ms. Equality at the bound is eligible (receipt + uncertainty exactly == D passes; 1 ms later fails).
failure_behavior: Unknown, unmeasured, excessive (> bound), or internally inconsistent uncertainty makes the observation INVALID for point-in-time eligibility (it remains in the evidence store, counted, unusable). The bound may not be adjusted after observing test outcomes without a separate documented principal review.
measurement_method: Per-observation: the capture host's clock-sync status and offset bound at capture time, recorded in the provenance envelope from the sync source (e.g. NTP/chrony estimate). In laboratory tests the uncertainty is supplied by the scripted clock-status provider, including UNKNOWN and excessive cases.
rationale: A healthy NTP-disciplined host holds offset far below 100 ms; 250 ms allows jitter headroom while remaining ~0.08% of the 300 s primary decision offset and 0.4% of the 60 s secondary offset, so the bound cannot materially move an eligibility decision. It is deliberately stricter than any plausible network/timestamp granularity in the evidence chain.
